text:
Sam K.: Heads-up — Verity Edge asked for a dedicated POC pool for their on-prem regulated workflow. They want EU region and H100 if possible. Need sizing recs and timeline.
Anya P.: Thanks. Quick details? expected qps, latency SLO, and if they need VPC/private plane or just VPC peering?
Sam K.: Initial POC: ~200 qps conversational <=200ms p95 for short chats (512 tokens). 3 devs + 1 SRE need API keys. Must be EU data residency (eu-west-1). They asked about burst to handle demo spikes.
Reza G.: H100 gives best perf but higher cost. Options: 4xH100 dedicated (predictable perf) or 8xA100-80GB mixed sku to trade cost for capacity. If they want headroom for spikes, we can enable burst pool (adds ephemeral capacity from a shared burst tier).
Mikaela S.: Security asks: SOC2? KMS key for encryption? private control plane? customers want IP allowlist + CIDR for VPC peering. We have to answer security questionnaire.
Sam K.: Correct — Verity needs org-level KMS + ability to rotate keys, and we must provide answers for encryption in transit & at rest. Also they want to know committed vs trial billing for the POC (30-day POC).
Anya P.: From sales side: we can offer a 30-day trial credit for Reserved capacity, but for Dedicated we typically require monthly commit for dedicated SKUs. For POC we can provision with a temporary waived commit — ops approval needed.
Reza G.: Technical ask: if we do 4xH100 in eu-west-1, expected throughput ~600 concurrent streaming tokens/s (depends on batching). For 512 token context with batching 8, p95 should be ~160-220ms. A100 option will increase latency but gives more concurrent sessions.
Mikaela S.: Network: We need their VPC CIDR and a target /28 for the pool peering. Also a set of allowed dev IPs for API key allowlist. Can someone post the minimal CIDR requirements?
Reza G.: Minimal: we require a /28 (16 addresses) for control plane peering and a separate /28 for model host interfaces if using Private deployment. For Dedicated (hosted in our tenant) we only need one /28 for peering.
Sam K.: Verity asked about example request/CLI to speed approvals. Reza can you drop a quick command they can hand to infra?
Reza G.: Sure, example (internal):
```
rictl pool create --name verity-edge-poc --region eu-west-1 \\
  --sku h100 --count 4 --burst-enabled true \\
  --vpc-peer-cidr 10.12.240.0/28 --kms-key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd1234 \\
  --contact email:verity-eng@verity.com
```
Sam K.: Perfect. I'll send that to their infra lead.
Mikaela S.: Ops checklist: 1) Confirm we can waive commit for 30-day POC 2) Approve burst for demo 3) Create org-level KMS policy 4) Prepare security questionnaire answers (SOC2, encryption, logging retention).
Anya P.: Sales note: they also asked about token-level cost estimate. Can eng provide a rough monthly spend estimate for both options (4xH100 vs 8xA100) at expected 200 qps?
Reza G.: Rough calc (very rough): at 200 qps * 3600 * 24 * 30 sessions with avg 150 tokens per request -> tokens/month ~200 * 3600 * 24 * 30 * 150 ~ 777,600,000 tokens. H100 route cost will be higher per GPU-hour. I'll ping Fin for a proper quote but ballpark: 4xH100 reserved ~€XXk/month; 8xA100 ~€YYk/month.
InfraBot: Pool provisioning request received. Ticket #POC-9271. ETA: ops review in 1 business day.
Sam K.: Re: timeline — can we provision within 48 hours once CIDR + PoC approver + billing contact provided?
Mikaela S.: Yes, ops can spin up a 4xH100 test pool in eu-west-1 within 48-72 hours after we get signed approval and CIDR. Burst enablement may add 24 hours.
Anya P.: I'll compile security questionnaire answers and send to Verity. Sam, can you get their PO/approver and the CIDR today?
Sam K.: Reached out to their infra lead, pasted the rictl snippet, and asked for CIDR + PO contact. Pinged in thread.
Verity Infra Lead (external): Thanks — we can provide 10.12.240.0/28 and dev IP allowlist. PO pending internal legal, should be with you tomorrow.
Sam K.: Great. Once we have PO and CIDR we'll ask ops to provision. Anything else?
Reza G.: One more: add a canary route and model pin config so we can rollback to smaller quantized variant automatically if latency spikes. I'll add the rollout policy to the pool config.
Mikaela S.: Noted — include canary + auto-fallback to quantized model. Also ensure logs capture token-level usage for cost audits.
Sam K.: Cool. I'll close the loop once PO arrives. :thumbsup:
